note: Each cleared course of the ziggurat reveals one fact about Mesopotamian temple-building. Every fact is drawn from real chapter text — 'basis' must appear in the source chapter (checked by tools/verify-ziggurat.js). Facts are revealed in order as courses rise.

facts.label: The house of the god
facts.fact: At the heart of every Mesopotamian city stood the house of its god — a statue fed, clothed, and housed as though alive.

facts.label: The stepped tower
facts.fact: That house was often crowned by a ziggurat — the great stepped platform-tower whose most famous survivor stands at Ur.

facts.label: Raised to the moon
facts.fact: The ziggurat of Ur was raised to the moon-god Nanna, who presided over the city.

facts.label: A statement in mud-brick
facts.fact: The ziggurat was a theological statement in mud-brick — the built claim that here the divine and human worlds meet.

facts.label: The mountain-house
facts.fact: Each great town was the household of its deity, its ziggurat the god's mountain-house; to neglect it was to invite the flood, the plague, the enemy.

facts.label: Etemenanki
facts.fact: The great ziggurat of Babylon bore the name Etemenanki — 'the House of the Foundation of Heaven and Earth.'

facts.label: The hinge of worlds
facts.basis: the hinge joining the divine and human worlds
facts.fact: Etemenanki was a built claim that the temple was the hinge joining the divine and human worlds — the point where the god descended.

facts.label: The first writing
facts.basis: the first true writing into wet clay
facts.fact: Around 3300 BCE, in the temple-city of Uruk, someone pressed the first true writing into wet clay — not to sing of gods, but to count.

facts.label: The first named author
facts.basis: the first author in human history known by name
facts.fact: Enheduanna, high priestess of Nanna at Ur, became the first author in human history known by name.

facts.label: Marduk's spring
facts.fact: Each spring at the Akitu, the Babylonian New Year, the Enuma Elish was recited to re-enthrone Marduk and renew the cosmos against chaos.

facts.label: The number of the gods
facts.fact: Each great deity held a number in the base-60 (sexagesimal) system Mesopotamia gave the world — Anu 60, Enlil 50, Sin the moon 30.

facts.label: The cities recovered
facts.basis: their ziggurats and temple accounts recovered
facts.fact: The temple-cities named in the literature — Uruk, Ur, Nippur, Eridu — have been dug, their ziggurats and temple accounts recovered.
